blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse applied to CPG & Brands. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

CPG brands compete on shelf, on shelf-image and on data: trade spend efficiency, retail execution truth, demand signal quality and now provenance claims. The brands that win industrialize the sell-side data relationship with retailers.

items: Retailer portals and EDI produce a patchwork; trade-spend ROI is estimated.
Promotions, distribution changes and retail signals confuse planners; forecast error compounds.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Advanced Risk & Predictive Analytics, Lakehouse Architecture & Migration, Master Data, Governance & Cataloging from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Trade promotion management, Demand planning, Retail execution) on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — EUDR among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Forward-looking risk on governed data: credit, insurance, operational and market models that explain themselves.
Turn the data estate into revenue: embedded analytics, data sharing and insight products with real P&L.
Resilient, observable pipelines: trusted data from source to decision at SLA.
Retailer feeds harmonized for trade and demand analytics (trade ROI real)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Retail & Consumer Goods level this capability reads as: retailer-brand joint measurement without data leakage (incrementality verified per campaign). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
